metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Malaysia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports results from the PISA 2022 assessment administered in 81 countries and economies, including Malaysia. The analysis is based on PISA’s complex sampling design of students within schools, and OECD typically uses sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and correct standard errors for the design. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name(s) or whether replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported uncertainty intervals (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicate that the complex design was accounted for in the estimation of means and differences, even though the specific weight codes are not shown here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 creative thinking results and related descriptive comparisons (means, proficiency levels, relative success, and subgroup gaps) rather than reporting an ML model that requires explicit PV-combining rules. The factsheet also does not describe any missing-data strategy (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) because it is a high-level results communication rather than a methodological paper detailing data processing. As a result, the missing-data handling approach is not documented in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Malaysia is described as 7,069 students in 199 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, and for whom creative thinking results are reported in the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test context. The factsheet does not provide additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., specific task completion thresholds or missing-data exclusions), so the filtering criteria beyond the stated completion of the assessment are not specified.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for Malaysia (15-year-olds) within PISA 2022 Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools. Creative thinking is assessed with 32 open-ended tasks scored using human judgement and rubrics, covering three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Malaysia’s mean creative thinking score is 25/60, significantly below the OECD average (33), and students’ relative performance aligns with expectations from mathematics (and is above expectations from reading). The factsheet reports proficiency distribution (54% at Level 3+; 12% at Level 5–6) and within-Malaysia gaps by socio-economic status (10.3 score points between top and bottom quartiles) and gender (girls +3.3 points). It also highlights relative strengths in evaluating/improving ideas and higher proficiency in visual expression and social problem solving, while noting weaker performance in generating diverse ideas.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study: it does not specify any predictive modeling pipeline, algorithmic training, or target-variable prediction. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, PV-handling for model estimation, missing-data handling procedures, and structured ML findings are not applicable or not reported in the provided text. The factsheet instead communicates descriptive and comparative PISA outcomes (means, proficiency levels, relative success, and subgroup differences) using PISA’s underlying assessment and estimation framework.
